text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Slovenia newspapers:

- The rightist "Spring" alliance of opposition parties rejected prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek's coalition offer, saying it was too biased in favour of Drnovsek's centre-left Liberal Democrats..
- Slovenian truck drivers face difficulties when travelling to the former Soviet Union, the Balkans or the Middle East, the foreign ministry said.
- Troubled shoe factory Peko is working on an agreement with its creditor banks that may help save it from bankruptcy.
- U.S. military ship USS La Salle arrived in the Slovenian port of Koper where it will stay for five days.

- Slovenia's Constitutional Court ruled the former Yugoslav royal family, which fled the country during World War Two, had no claims on its former property in Slovenia. The property was nationalised in 1947 following the abolition of monarchy.
- The government has prepared a bill to set up a state mutual fund which would would provide compensation to employees of bankrupt companies.
- Recently-privatised petrol company Petrol boasts some 95,000 shareholders.
- Peter Hrescak, a former consultant to Maribor mayor Alojz Krizman, accused the mayor of corruption.
- Experts say the likelihood of a broad coaliton government that would include most parliamentary parties have become slim.
- At Monday's meeting of European Union foreign ministers in Brussels, Denmark called upon EU member parliaments for early ratification of Slovenia's association agreement with the 15-member bloc.
- In most newly privatised companies, the overall number of shareholders significantly decreased after they were listed on the Ljubljana bourse.
